subject: general
question: Anwar’s salary is ₹11,000 per month. He spends ₹6,000 on house rent and ₹3,000 on bills, and the rest of the amount is his monthly savings. Find his savings (in ₹) in a year, if in the month of his birthday, he spent all his monthly savings on birthday celebrations.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Monthly Salary = ₹11,000

Monthly Expenditure = ₹6,000 + ₹3,000 = ₹9,000

Monthly Savings = ₹11,000 − ₹9,000 = ₹2,000

Savings for 11 months (excluding birthday month) = ₹2,000 × 11 = ₹22,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹22,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Monthly Salary = **₹11,000**

House Rent = **₹6,000**

Bills = **₹3,000**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e7015a6ac2e17969d61718142f04aff107d233ebb5d7ee342f5d3bc234b020cf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Monthly Expenditure = 6,000 + 3,000 = **₹9,000**

⇒ Monthly Savings = 11,000 − 9,000 = **₹2,000**

⇒ Total Months in a year = **12**

⇒ Months in which he saves = 12 − 1 (Birthday Month) = **11 months**

⇒ Annual Savings = 2,000 × 11

⇒ Annual Savings = **₹22,000**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹22,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Concept

Income = **Expenditure** + **Savings**. Any increase in expenditure with constant income directly reduces savings.

Percentage Savings

Savings % = (**Savings** ÷ **Income**) × 100. In this case, monthly savings % = (2,000/11,000) × 100 ≈ 18.18%.

Annual Calculation

When a specific month's savings are spent, subtract that month's value or simply calculate for the remaining 11 months.
